findings: Initial Llama 3.3 recovery drafted a command with an empty output and no URL; initial Haiku recovery copied an example URL the user did not supply. The final input guard rejects these; offline replay preserves the original outcomes separately.

Haiku correction yields useful contribution/template and workflow guidance, but copied command inputs and remaining rejections prevent selecting it on the initial pass count alone.
Sonnet recovered an option-value distinction, but its accepted release-version answer still incorrectly suggests the current PyPI release will align with main. That remains a semantic blocker.

summary.text: Use the acquire http command to download a file over HTTP into a local output file.

details.text: The acquire http command fetches a file via HTTP(S) to a local path.
You can specify the output file name using the --output option.

nextSteps.text: To download a file, provide the URL and the desired output file name.

summary.text: Use the acquire http command to download a file from an HTTP(S) URL into a local output file by specifying the source URL as a positional argument and the destination path with the --output option.

details.text: The acquire http command (also available as import http) accepts an HTTP(S) URL and saves it to a local file.
The --output option designates the local destination file path where the downloaded content will be written.

nextSteps.text: For multiple file downloads, use --inputs to provide a list of URLs or --manifest to reference a YAML/JSON file containing batch download specifications.
For authenticated access, use --auth, --header, or --credential options to pass credentials or custom headers required by the remote server.

summary.text: Commands documented at the pinned main revision may not match an older installed release. Zyra is distributed via PyPI and its CLI surface can change between releases, so main-branch examples risk flag-not-found or subcommand-missing errors on older installs. Check your installed version before relying on those examples.

details.text: The evidence is read from a specific commit on main. Zyra is installable from PyPI and the CLI commands documented at that revision reflect only that pinned state, not necessarily your older release.

The CLI index at the pinned revision lists domains including acquire, decide, disseminate, narrate, process, run, search, simulate, transform, verify, and visualize, plus aliases. An older release may have a subset of these or different option spellings.
Whether a specific command or option from the main-branch docs works on your older version cannot be confirmed without knowing your installed version and the corresponding release tag.

nextSteps.text: Find your installed Zyra version by asking your environment directly, then compare it to the PyPI release history to identify which tag your version corresponds to.
Once you know your installed version tag, ask this advisor to look up a specific command against that revision so you get accurate command and option information for your release rather than main.
If you want to use the latest commands from the main-branch documentation, upgrading your install to the current PyPI release would align your environment with that documented CLI surface.

selectionDecision.reason: The comparison exposes accepted unsupported advice and command-input failures, while the focused final guards still reject many ordinary command answers. No model is selected by delivery, size or cost alone. Runtime selection remains explicit.
